challenge.method: Opened each named source once in a separate connector call. Checked the pinned paths and reported capture metadata, then compared the publisher passage with the decoded SPDX licenseText and the standalone text. Checked the year and named issuer, the permission grant, each numbered restriction, and the complete disclaimer. Examined the text immediately after the disclaimer and the SPDX cross-reference flag for evidence against the claimed scope.
challenge.results: All three captures show the same 2017 Jordan Ritter attribution, operative wording, and disclaimer. JSON escaping decodes to the same apostrophes, and the extra blank line in the detail leaves the wording unchanged. The publisher's separate tcpkill introduction places the Dug Song notice outside the stated span. The false cross-reference flag concerns the master-branch URL and does not contradict the observed correspondence at the pinned path.

limitations: The comparison covers only the Jordan Ritter passage in the exact captures. The later Dug Song notice, legal equivalence, rights for other works, text reuse, and installation are outside its scope.

The captures establish the pinned paths and displayed content. The numeric release labels came from the candidate records and were not independently authenticated through tag metadata. The policy commit and bundle digest were treated as supplied review identifiers.
